text.en: MOLECULAR DYNAMICS / THERMOSTATS Thermostats: temperature control and distributions Compare fluctuations, ergodicity and time correlations as well as mean temperature, from Nosé–Hoover and velocity rescaling to stochastic and momentum-conserving methods. Retain the earlier two-method comparison of Langevin and CSVR. Preserve the earlier one-degree-of-freedom harmonic Langevin/BAOAB case. A separate edition compares both baths with the same OBABO splitting for a nondegenerate two-degree harmonic system and a two-degree anharmonic system with quartic coefficient lambda=0.2, and checks the standalone CSVR kinetic-energy kernel. A separate fixed two-mode release contrasts direct rescaling, Berendsen, Nosé–Hoover and NHC3 while retaining unmet or unresolved original goals. The remaining six methods are planned. JSON · Markdown Define the controlled temperature With kinetic energy K and f active degrees of freedom, the kinetic temperature is T = 2 K / (f k_B). Count constraints and removed center-of-mass motion consistently, and separate thermal motion from streaming. State whether rotational degrees of freedom are included. Equal mean temperature does not imply equal distributions For f independent momentum degrees of freedom with classical quadratic kinetic energy, canonical equilibrium gives 2 K/(k_B T₀) a chi-square distribution with f degrees of freedom. Its mean K is f k_B T₀/2 and variance is f(k_B T₀)²/2. Direct rescaling v ← √(T₀/T) v fixes K immediately after application, removing these fluctuations. CSVR instead uses a stochastic factor to generate fluctuations. Separate sampling from dynamics An invariant distribution does not ensure adequate finite-time exploration. Even correct equilibrium sampling can coexist with friction- or collision-induced changes in velocity autocorrelations and diffusion. Assess integration error, heat-bath coupling time and random-seed dependence. CSVR and Langevin: shared canonical targets, distinct correlations The new comparison is limited to small classical systems. CSVR and Langevin use matched OBABO splitting, degrees of freedom, temperature, potential and observation times. Distribution, fluctuations and correlations are separate diagnostics. The earlier BAOAB harmonic results remain in their original release. The stochastic CSVR update and its sign CSVR evolves the total kinetic energy stochastically and scales all momenta together. The implementation uses the 2007 kinetic-energy SDE and exact propagator, with the signed factor in the 2008 paper. Here h denotes a thermostat substep. The same Gaussian R determines energy and sign. Momentum flips matter for a few degrees of freedom. Draw S directly from a chi-square law with f−1 degrees, with S=0 at f=1; this avoids the Gamma-construction typo identified by the original author. dK=Kˉ−Kτ dt+2KKˉfτ dW c=e−h/τ,a=(1−c)Kˉf,K+=(cK+a R)2+aS,R∼N(0,1),S∼χf−12 α=sign⁡ ⁣(cK+a R)K+/K,pi+=αpi Sources: Canonical sampling through velocity rescaling · Stochastic thermostats: comparison of local and global schemes · Algorithms: stochastic velocity rescaling, author correction note Compare with the same splitting Both new methods use O(Δt/2)–B(Δt/2)–A(Δt)–B(Δt/2)–O(Δt/2) for MD step Δt: A moves coordinates, B applies forces and O is the thermostat. The CSVR formula uses bath substep h=Δt/2. They share a velocity-Verlet core and differ in the bath updates. Set τ=(2γ)⁻¹ to match kinetic-energy relaxation for the force-free bath. This τ is not the friction time γ⁻¹. At f=1, signed CSVR has the Langevin transition law; a paired-noise check tests the implementation. The earlier BAOAB example uses a different B–A–O–A–B splitting. Its release and independent linear reference remain unchanged; the new OBABO references and errors do not replace them. τ=(2γ)−1,p+=e−γhp+mkBT0(1−e−2γh) Rphys(f=1) Sources: Stochastic thermostats: comparison of local and global schemes Three separate questions: distribution, fluctuation and correlation Both methods share the static canonical target. Check momentum, kinetic energy and instantaneous-temperature distributions, means and variances. Position references are analytic for harmonic systems and use separate quadrature for the anharmonic case. Matching the mean temperature alone does not check fluctuations. Dynamic correlations depend on the method and coupling time. Measure position q, momentum p, kinetic energy K and total energy H without requiring agreement between methods. For harmonic Langevin, distinguish the continuous matrix exponential from the OBABO discrete stationary covariance/propagator. Other full-system correlations are measured with uncertainty and timestep dependence. The exact ρK(t)=exp(−t/τ) reference applies only to the isolated bath. Full harmonic or anharmonic motion exchanges K and U, so that expression is not used as its correlation target. CDF errors are maxima over predeclared checkpoints: five position/energy points and, for the conditional bath, three quantile points. They are not Kolmogorov–Smirnov suprema over the whole distribution. Full-system correlations use canonical-reference centering and normalization, so finite-step zero-lag values need not equal one exactly. K=∑i=1fpi22mi,Kˉ=fkBT02,Tinst=2KfkB 2KkBT0∼χf2,Var⁡K=f(kBT0)22,Var⁡Tinst=2T02f CX(t)=⟨(X(t)−⟨X⟩)(X(0)−⟨X⟩)⟩,ρX(t)=CX(t)/CX(0) E[K+∣K]=cK+fa,Var⁡(K+∣K)=2fa2+4acK,ρK(t)=e−t/τ (bath only) Sampling limits and implementation boundaries Preservation from a canonical initial ensemble and relaxation from temperature-perturbed starts are distinct checks. Use independent replicas, fixed seeds and finite observation windows; separate sampling uncertainty from timestep and coupling effects. These small tests do not guarantee mixing from arbitrary starts. Correlation standard errors use the spread of products across independent replicas at each lag; they are not uncertainties of a single-trajectory time average or an effective-sample-size estimate. No independent dynamical reference is claimed for the anharmonic full-system correlations, which are not presented as having zero error. A common scaling factor does not directly randomize momentum direction. A correct K distribution cannot rule out restricted sampling from invariant conditions such as zero total momentum in a symmetric system, or from invariant subspaces. The adopted degrees of freedom include no added constraints or removed center-of-mass mode. For a positive bath step, at K=0 the direction is undefined, so this implementation rejects global rescaling explicitly. It does not inject an arbitrary direction as an undocumented algorithm. Nonfinite or nonphysical parameters are also checked. Sources: Canonical sampling through velocity rescaling Primary sources for the adopted equations G. Bussi, D. Donadio and M. Parrinello (2007). Canonical sampling through velocity rescaling · DOI: 10.1063/1.2408420 Checked author-manuscript sections II.1–II.3, kinetic SDE (7), and appendix A (16)–(22); consult the author correction for Gamma-based squared-noise generation. G. Bussi and M. Parrinello (2008). Stochastic thermostats: comparison of local and global schemes · DOI: 10.1016/j.cpc.2008.01.006 Checked manuscript sections I–II, τ=(2γ)⁻¹, finite-step (8)–(9) and f=1; bibliography cross-checked with SISSA. Giovanni Bussi (2026). Algorithms: stochastic velocity rescaling, author correction note Checked the author note identifying the 2007 Gamma-generation typo. Year denotes access, not the correction publication year. Compare NH1,NHC3,Berendsen and fixed-speed baths at two couplings/two steps with256canonical and128heated replicas. Separately test physical reversal,Hext derivative,phi1,local weak-coupling inverses and noninjective rescaling. Retain four distributions,fluctuations,signed correlations and unresolved DKW precision at time20. This authored splitting is not a full LAMMPS/MKT reproduction. Time20does not prove mixing/equilibration; correct mean temperature alone does not establish canonical sampling or general ergodicity. Measurements, unmet/unresolved original goals, code and checks Fixed-input thermostat and small-model coupling cases Compare bath choices under the same OBABO splitting; separate step/coupling effects and independent-stream sampling uncertainty. Check distributions and temperature fluctuations separately from correlations. Langevin and CSVR correlations need not agree: they describe method-dependent sampling dynamics. Langevin thermostat: canonical distributions, timestep bias and correlation · ZIP · Stored results · Rerun receipt Distribution checks use a harmonic potential and fixed seeds. Exact position variance does not remove finite-step momentum bias. Evidence does not transfer to other thermostats, general molecules or long ab initio MD. Exact CSVR bath: conditional laws, fluctuations and kinetic correlation · ZIP · Stored results · Rerun receipt A bath diagnostic, not another independent physical problem. Correct K sampling does not thermalize momentum directions by global scaling alone. The bath-only exp(−t/tau) identity is not a full-MD kinetic ACF. Statistical decisions apply to fixed seeds/budgets, not general mixing guarantees. CSVR versus Langevin: distributions, fluctuations and correlations of two harmonic modes · ZIP · Stored results · Rerun receipt Global-CSVR and local-Langevin dynamical correlations are not required to agree. CDF errors are maxima over five declared points, not whole-line KS distances. Canonical-start preservation and the heated-start finite-time check do not prove ergodicity; tests retain an invariant unexcited-axis counterexample. No extrapolation to molecules, constraints or BOMD. Anharmonic CSVR versus Langevin: distribution checks against Boltzmann quadrature · ZIP · Stored results · Rerun receipt A small example for one separable two-mode quartic potential and fixed seeds. H is not treated as harmonic Gamma. No independent exact full-system dynamical reference is claimed, and neither matching correlations nor time order hidden by sampling noise is an acceptance claim. Molecular transport, quantum and ab initio MD are outside scope. A two-state BO / CP-type model with a short nuclear thermostat coupling · ZIP · Stored results · Rerun receipt Long first-principles NVE and general electronic/nuclear thermostat equilibration remain deferred. No material prediction, multi-orbital CPMD or canonical/ergodic sampling certificate. NH,chains,weak coupling and fixed-speed contrasts · ZIP · Stored results · Rerun receipt This authored splitting is not a full LAMMPS/MKT reproduction. Time20does not prove mixing/equilibration; correct mean temperature alone does not establish canonical sampling or general ergodicity. Constraints,centre-of-mass removal and canonical statistics · ZIP · Stored results · Rerun receipt These fixed linear constraints do not cover nonlinear molecular constraints,Fixman corrections or transport coefficients. Redundant systems with independent seeds need not have identical paths; CSVR dynamical correlations are empirical. Eight foundational entries Direct velocity rescaling Multiply velocities by a common factor to set the kinetic energy at each application. Simple deterministic rescaling does not reproduce canonical kinetic-energy fluctuations. A comparison case for distinguishing temperature control from canonical sampling. Ratio-based rescaling is undefined at T=0; the application interval also matters. Other names: ベロシティースケーリング / ベロシティスケーリング / velocity scaling / simple velocity rescaling Method status, JSON and Markdown GROMACS: temperature coupling Berendsen weak-coupling thermostat Relax the temperature difference over a chosen coupling time using velocity scaling. Fluctuations are suppressed, so this is not a correct canonical sampler. Treat as a historical relaxation method; do not assume correct NVT fluctuations or response properties. (1984), Molecular dynamics with coupling to an external bath GROMACS: temperature coupling Andersen thermostat Represent stochastic heat-bath collisions by redrawing selected particle velocities from a Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution. Canonical sampling and physical time correlations are separate criteria. Independent velocity redraws alter total momentum and transport. Other names: アンダーセン / stochastic collisions Method status, JSON and Markdown Andersen (1980), Molecular dynamics simulations at constant pressure and/or temperature GROMACS: temperature coupling Langevin thermostat Langevin thermostat: canonical distributions, timestep bias and correlation: Compare harmonic BAOAB with canonical and discrete-Lyapunov stationary distributions, and with continuous/discrete time correlations. CSVR versus Langevin: distributions, fluctuations and correlations of two harmonic modes: Compare global CSVR with local Langevin on two nondegenerate modes using the same OBABO splitting. Record position, momentum, temperature and total-energy distributions, fluctuations and correlations. Anharmonic CSVR versus Langevin: distribution checks against Boltzmann quadrature: Compare CSVR and Langevin distributions, temperature/energy fluctuations and correlations for two weakly quartic modes. Independent Boltzmann quadrature provides equilibrium references. Friction changes dynamical correlations and diffusion. Finite-step sampling errors must be assessed together with the integration scheme. Distinguish the original extended Hamiltonian from the real-time Nosé–Hoover equations. An invariant distribution alone does not establish ergodicity. Other names: ノセ / 能勢 / Nose thermostat / extended system Method status, JSON and Markdown Nosé (1984), A unified formulation of the constant temperature molecular dynamics methods Nosé–Hoover thermostat A deterministic method with a dynamically adjusted heat-bath friction variable. The canonical distribution is invariant, but small systems can fail to explore it ergodically. Check nonergodicity in systems such as harmonic oscillators and dependence on bath mass or coupling time. Mean temperature is insufficient validation. This extension addresses sampling problems of a single thermostat. Chain length, masses and substeps matter. Adding a chain does not universally guarantee ergodicity. Distinguish fixed kinetic energy from the fluctuating canonical kinetic energy at finite system size. Configurational and full phase-space distributions differ. Separate classical equilibrium fluctuation–dissipation settings from nonequilibrium approximations to nuclear quantum effects; neither is an electronic-structure solver. Standard symmetric pair forces conserve the pair’s total momentum. Relevant when momentum transport matters. Verify matched friction/noise, radial weights and finite-step effects. Other names: 散逸粒子動力学 / dissipative particle dynamics / pairwise thermostat Method status, JSON and Markdown Español & Warren (1995), Statistical Mechanics of Dissipative Particle Dynamics LAMMPS: pair_style dpd / dpd/tstat Lowe–Andersen thermostat Stochastically redraw a component of a nearby pair’s relative velocity while preserving the pair’s center-of-mass momentum. Distinguish from independent-particle Andersen collisions. Collision frequency and neighbor radius affect transport such as viscosity and diffusion. Other names: ロウ・アンダーセン / Lowe Andersen Method status, JSON and Markdown Lowe (1999), An alternative approach to dissipative particle dynamics Validated scope and next checks Three new cases separate the exact isolated-bath law, a few-degree harmonic system and a weakly anharmonic system. Each entry exposes fixed inputs, measurements, errors/uncertainty, criteria, code, tests, ZIP and independent-extraction receipt. The earlier BAOAB example is separate evidence. These CSVR comparisons are not evidence for other algorithms. A separate fixed-input release contrasts four deterministic schemes and retains unmet/unresolved original goals; six other schemes remain planned. Sources and review scope For CSVR, the kinetic-energy equations/appendix in the 2007 author manuscript, signed update in the 2008 manuscript and author correction were checked. The adopted small classical examples are validated by separate references, quadrature and actual reruns. They do not reproduce the original Lennard–Jones or TIP4P-water experiments. This CSVR source audit is not transferred to other algorithms. Four deterministic schemes have a separate limited release; the remaining six schemes are comparative reading and primary-source entry points. Individual original-paper curation for Gaussian isokinetic remains open. Citation and reuse · Method registry / JSON
